journal.text: the judgment is affrmed under 28 U. S. C. § 2109, which provides that under these circumstances “the court shall enter its order affrming the judgment of the court from which the case was brought for review with the same effect as upon affrmance by an equally divided court.” Justice Thomas, Justice Alito, Justice Gorsuch, Justice Kavanaugh and Justice Barrett took no part in the consideration or decision of this petition.

journal.text: Petitions for rehearing denied. Attorney Discipline No. D–3094. In the Matter of Disbarment of Michael Steven Arif. Michael Steven Arif, of Falls Church, Virginia, having been suspended from the practice of law in this Court by order of December 5, 2022; and a rule having been issued requiring him to show cause why he should not be disbarred; and the time to fle a response having expired; It is ordered that Michael Steven Arif is disbarred from the practice of law in this Court. No. D–3102. In the Matter of Disbarment of Felipe Nery Gomez. Felipe Nery Gomez, of Chicago, Illinois, having been suspended from the practice of law in this Court by order of December 12, 2022; and a rule having been issued requiring him to show cause why he should not be disbarred; and the time to fle a response having expired; It is ordered that Felipe Nery Gomez is disbarred from the practice of law in this Court. No. D–3109. In the Matter of Disbarment of Jack Revels Tucker Jordan. Motion for reconsideration of disbarment denied. No. D–3122. In the Matter of Discipline of Kiran Nargis Thara Meettook. Kiran Nargis Thara Meettook, of New York, New York, is suspended from the practice of law in this Court, and a rule will issue, returnable within 40 days, requiring her to show cause why she should not be disbarred from the practice of law in this Court. No. D–3123. In the Matter of Discipline of Mary Lee Pilla. Mary Lee Pilla, of Novelty, Ohio, is suspended from the practice of law in this Court, and a rule will issue, returnable within 40 days, requiring her to show cause why she should not be disbarred from the practice of law in this Court. journal.case: Ashley Moody, Attorney General of Florida, et al., Petitioners v. NetChoice, LLC, dba NetChoice, et al

NetChoice, LLC, dba NetChoice, et al., Petitioners v. Ken Paxton, Attorney General of Texas. The following briefng schedule is adopted: Respondents in No. 22-277 and petitioners in No. 22-555 shall fle opening briefs on the merits on or before Thursday, November 30, 2023, and the briefs are to bear a light blue cover. Any brief of an amicus curiae in support or in support of neither party shall be fled on or before Thursday, December 7, 2023, and the brief shall bear a light green cover. Petitioners in No. 22-277 and respondents in No. 22- 555 shall fle response briefs on the merits on or before Tuesday, January 16, 2024, and the briefs are to bear a light red cover. Any brief of an amicus curiae in support shall be fled on or before Tuesday, January 23, 2024, and the brief shall bear a dark green cover. Reply briefs are to be fled in compliance with Rule 25.3, and the briefs are to bear a yellow cover. An amicus curiae shall fle only a single brief in these cases

journal.text: Application for stay presented to Justice Alito and by him referred to the Court granted. The preliminary injunction issued on July 4, 2023 by the United States District Court for the Western District of Louisiana, case No. 3:22-cv-01213, as modifed by the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit on October 3, 2023, case No. 23-30445, is stayed. The application for stay is also treated as a petition for a writ of certiorari, and the petition is granted on the questions presented in the application. The stay shall terminate upon the sending down of the judgment of this Court. Justice Alito, with whom Justice Thomas and Justice Gorsuch join, dissenting from grant of application for stay.

journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.case: Katherine K. Vidal, Under Secretary of Commerce for Intellectual Property and Director, United States Patent and Trademark Offce, Petitioner v. Steve Elster.
journal.text: Argued by Mr. Deputy Solicitor General Malcolm L. Stewart for the petitioner, and by Mr. Jonathan E. Taylor for the respondent. The Chief Justice said: “Mr. Stewart, our records refect that this was your 100th oral argument before the Court. You are the fourth to reach this rare milestone this century. “Throughout your career, you have consistently advocated positions on behalf of the United States in an exemplary manner. “I recall one case from my days in private practice 23 years ago in which I was counsel for petitioner and you argued in support of respondent. When the opinion came down, I was just nine votes short of a unanimous result for my client. “On behalf of the Court, I extend to you our appreciation for your advocacy before the Court and dedicated service as an offcer of this Court. We look forward to hearing from you many more times.” Adjourned until Monday, November 6, 2023, at 10 o'clock.

journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the District Court of Appeal of Florida, Fourth District dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.case: Jason Payne, Petitioner v. Joseph R. Biden, Jr., President of the United States, et al.
journal.text: On petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. Petition for writ of certiorari granted. Judgment vacated, and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit with instructions to dismiss the case as moot. See United States v. Munsingwear, Inc., 340 U. S. 36 (1950). Justice Jackson, concurring: Although I would require that the party seeking vacatur establish equitable entitlement to that remedy, I accede to vacatur here based on the Court's established practice when the mootness occurs through the unilateral action of the party that prevailed in the lower court. See Acheson Hotels, LLC v. Laufer, 601 U. S. ––– (2023) (Jackson, J., concurring in the judgment).
journal.case: Joseph R. Biden, Jr., President of the United States, et al., Petitioners v. Feds for Medical Freedom, et al.
journal.text: On petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. Petition for writ of certiorari granted. Judgment vacated, and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit with instructions to direct the District Court to vacate as moot its order granting a preliminary injunction. See United States v. Munsingwear, Inc., 340 U. S. 36 (1950). Justice Jackson, dissenting: In my view, the party seeking vacatur has not established equitable entitlement to that remedy. See Acheson Hotels, LLC v. Laufer, 601 U. S. ––– (2023) (Jackson, J., concurring in the judgment).

journal.text: the applications for stay presented to The Chief Justice and by him referred to the Court deferred pending oral argument. The applications are consolidated, and a total of 1 hour is allotted for oral argument. The applications will be set for argument in the February 2024 argument session. journal.text: Petition for writ of certiorari to the Supreme Court of Colorado granted. The case is set for oral argument on Thursday, February 8, 2024. Petitioner's brief on the merits, and any amicus curiae briefs in support or in support of neither party, are to be fled on or before Thursday, January 18, 2024. Respondents' briefs on the merits, and any amicus curiae briefs in support, are to be fled on or before Wednesday, January 31, 2024. The reply brief, if any, is to be fled on or before 5 p.m., Monday, February 5 2024.
journal.case: (23A469). Mike Moyle, Speaker of the Idaho House of Representatives, et al., Petitioners v. United States

(23A470). Idaho, Petitioner v. United States. Applications for stay presented to Justice Kagan and by her referred to the Court granted. The preliminary injunction issued on August 24, 2022, by the United States District Court for the District of Idaho, case
:22-cv-00329, is stayed.
journal.text: The applications for stay are also treated as petitions for writs of certiorari before judgment, and the petitions are granted on the question presented in Idaho's application. The cases are consolidated and a total of 1 hour is allotted for oral argument. The Clerk is directed to establish a briefng schedule that will allow the case to be argued in the April 2024 argument session. The stay shall terminate upon the sending down of the judgment of this Court.

journal.text: the judgment is affrmed under 28 U. S. C. § 2109, which provides that under these circumstances “the court shall enter its order affrming the judgment of the court from which the case was brought for review with the same effect as upon affrmance by an equally divided court.” The Chief Justice, Justice Thomas, Justice Alito, Justice Gorsuch, Justice Kavanaugh, and Justice Barrett took no part in the consideration or decision of this petition.

journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam). Mandamus Denied

journal.case: (23A745). Donald J. Trump, Applicant v. United States.
journal.text: Application for stay presented to The Chief Justice referred by him to the Court. The Special Counsel's request to treat the stay application as a petition for writ of certiorari is granted, and that petition is granted limited to the following question: Whether and if so to what extent does a former President enjoy presidential immunity from criminal prosecution for conduct alleged to involve offcial acts during his tenure in offce. Without expressing a view on the merits, this Court directs the Court of Appeals to continue withholding issuance of the mandate until the sending down of the judgment of this Court. Application for stay dismissed as moot. The case will be set for oral argument during the week of April 22, 2024. Petitioner's brief on the merits, and any amicus curiae briefs in support or in support of neither party, are to be fled on or before Tuesday, March 19, 2024. Respondent's brief on the merits, and any amicus curiae briefs in support, are to be fled on or before Monday, April 8, 2024. The reply brief, if any, is to be fled on or before 5 p.m., Monday, April 15, 2024.
journal.case: Speech First, Inc., Petitioner v. Timothy Sands, Individually and in His Offcial Capacity as President of Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University.
journal.text: On petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit. Petition for writ of certiorari granted. Judgment with respect to the Bias Policy claims vacated, and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit with instructions to dismiss those claims as moot. See United States v. Munsingwear, Inc., 340 U. S. 36 (1950). Justice Jackson, dissenting: I would deny the petition. In my view, the party seeking vacatur has not established entitlement to that remedy. See Acheson Hotels, LLC v. Laufer, 601 U.S. 1 (2023) (Jackson, J., concurring in the judgment). Justice Thomas, with whom Justice Alito joins, dissenting. Orders in Pending Cases

journal.case: In Re Solomon Roberts, Petitioner.
journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of habeas corpus dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.case: Raul Labrador, Attorney General of Idaho, Applicant v. Pam Poe, By and Through Her Parents and Next Friends, Penny and Peter Poe, et al.
journal.text: Application for stay presented to Justice Kagan and by her referred to the Court granted. The December 26, 2023 order of the United States District Court for the District of Idaho, case
journal.case: :23-cv-269, is stayed, except as to the provision to the plaintiffs of the treatments they sought below, pending the disposition of
journal.text: the appeal in the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit and disposition of a petition for a writ of certiorari, if such a writ is timely sought. Should certiorari be denied, this stay shall terminate automatically. In the event certiorari is granted, the stay shall terminate upon the sending down of the judgment of this Court. Justice Kagan would deny the application for stay. Justice Gorsuch, with whom Justice Thomas and Justice Alito join, concurring in the grant of stay. Justice Kavanaugh, with whom Justice Barrett joins, concurring in the grant of stay. Justice Jackson, with whom Justice Sotomayor joins, dissenting from grant of stay.

journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam). Habeas Corpus Denied

journal.case: Press Robinson, et al., Applicants v. Phillip Callais, et al

Nancy Landry, Secretary of State of Louisiana, et al., Applicants v. Phillip Callais, et al. Applications for stay presented to Justice Alito and by him referred to the Court granted. See Purcell v. Gonzalez, 549 U. S. 1 (2006). The April 30, 2024 order of the United States District Court for the Western District of Louisiana, case
:24–cv–00122, is stayed pending the timely docketing of
journal.text: the appeal in this Court. Should the jurisdictional statement be timely fled, this order shall remain in effect pending this Court's action on the appeal. If the appeal is dismissed, or the judgment affrmed, this order shall terminate automatically. In the event jurisdiction is noted or postponed, this order will remain in effect pending the sending down of the judgment of this Court. Justice Sotomayor and Justice Kagan would deny the applications for stay. Justice Jackson, dissenting from grant of applications for stay.

journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.case: In Re Kinley MacDonald, Petitioner.
journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of habeas corpus dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam). Mandamus Denied

journal.text: Petitions for rehearing denied. Attorney Discipline No. D–3137. In the Matter of Disbarment of Denis Charles Englisby. Denis Charles Englisby, of Chesterfeld, Virginia, having been suspended from the practice of law in this Court by order of April 29, 2024; and a rule having been issued and served upon him requiring him to show cause why he should not be disbarred; and a response having been fled; It is ordered that Denis Charles Englisby is disbarred from the practice of law in this Court. journal.case: Donald J. Trump, Petitioner v. United States.
journal.text: On writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. Judgment vacated and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit for further proceedings consistent with the opinion of this Court. Opinion by The Chief Justice. Concurring opinion by Justice Thomas. Opinion by Justice Barrett, concurring in part. Dissenting opinion announced by Justice Sotomayor, with whom Justice Kagan and Justice Jackson join. Dissenting opinion by Justice Jackson. Statement from The Chief Justice The Chief Justice said: “I am authorized to announce that the Court has acted upon all cases submitted to the Court for decision this Term. Disposition of items scheduled for Conference today will be reflected on an order list that will be released at nine thirty tomorrow morning. “The Court will be in recess from today until the first Monday in October 2024, at which time the October 2023 Term of the Court will be adjourned, and the October 2024 Term of the Court will begin, as provided by law. “On behalf of my colleagues, I thank the Supreme Court employees for their outstanding work and dedication to their important responsibilities during this term. The commitment and professionalism of all Court staff contributes significantly to the accomplishment of the Court’s mission. “The Court also thanks the members of the Court’s bar for their professionalism and cooperation. “Before we rise for the summer, I would like to note the retirement of six Court employees. “Private First Class Brian Porter retired on December 31, 2023, having served 23 years as a Supreme Court Police Officer. Kimberly Kiely retired from the Library on September 30, 2023, with 26 years of Supreme Court service. Janimel Scott retired from the Marshal’s Office on December 30, 2023, with 27 years of Supreme Court service. John Kouros retired from the Marshal’s Office on December 30, 2023, with 29 years of Supreme Court service. Clayton Higgins retired from the Clerk’s Office with 36 years of Supreme Court service. “And finally, Curator Catherine Fitts—an officer of the Court— retired on December 30, 2023, with 37 years of Supreme Court service. Catherine’s tireless efforts to record and preserve the history of the Court—through documents and physical objects—will benefit the Court for as long as it sits. “Mr. Porter, Ms. Kiely, Ms. Scott, Mr. Kouros, Mr. Higgins, and Ms. Fitts, we are grateful for your many years of hard work and dedication to the Court. We wish each of you well in your retirement. “Lastly, we would like to extend a warm welcome to David Mao, who today assumes his duties as the 12th Librarian of the court, and to express the Court’s gratitude to acting Librarian Bill Sleeman for his exemplary performance in that role over the past two years.” Adjourned until Monday, October 7, 2024, at 10 o’clock.

journal.text: Application for stay presented to Justice Kagan and by her referred to the Court granted in part and denied in part. The district court's May 2, 2024 judgment is stayed only to the extent it enjoins enforcement of Ariz. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 16-121.01(C) (2023) pending disposition of the appeals in the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit and disposition of a petition for writ of certiorari, if any such writ is timely sought. Should certiorari be denied, this stay shall terminate automatically. In the event certiorari is granted, the stay shall terminate upon the sending down of the judgment of this Court. The application is denied as to Ariz. Rev. Stat. Ann. §§ 16-121.01(E) and 16-127(A). Justice Thomas, Justice Alito, and Justice Gorsuch would grant the application in full. Justice Sotomayor, Justice Kagan, Justice Barrett, and Justice Jackson would deny the application in full.
